objective: Introduce Slayer Prime as the bounded enforcement control plane beneath Guardian authorization without changing the F00-F07 topology or sovereign authority hierarchy.

conflicts.originalConflict: Historical Slayer documentation described Slayer as Level 1 and referenced the stale core/slayer path.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Normalize Slayer to Level 2 enforcement/diagnostic responsibility, use the current core/slayers path, and make Slayer Prime the explicit enforcement subsystem.

conflicts.originalConflict: Legacy Slayer behavior mixed detection/case creation with the intended enforcement boundary.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Keep the existing Slayer swarm for detection and investigation while introducing Prime for authorized containment mutation, fencing, execution receipts, and postcondition proof.

changes: Added Slayer Prime contracts for incidents, evidence, action intents, authorization grants, action leases, containment proofs, and enforcement receipts.
Added evidence quorum with freshness, trust, and independent evidence-class requirements.
Added action policy with graduated scope and Guardian/Human authorization binding.
Added separate Slayer action lease with monotonic fencing token.
Added transactional enforcement executor with authoritative postcondition verification.
Added executable REVOKE_LEASE adapter backed by the existing LeaseManager.
Rejected unsupported physical enforcement actions instead of simulating success.
Wired canonical Slayer observations into Slayer Prime.
Wired Slayer Prime into SlayerEngine lifecycle and parallelized specialized patrol execution.
Updated Slayer hierarchy documentation and added Slayer Prime .okf contract.
notes: No floor topology or sovereign authority change was introduced.
Slayer Prime is an enforcement boundary, not a cognitive authority; Ascalon/AER cannot grant Prime authority.
Only REVOKE_LEASE is currently backed by a real runtime adapter.
FENCE, ISOLATE, TERMINATE, FLOOR_HALT, and FACTORY_HALT remain adapter-gated and are not claimed as physically implemented.
The action lease store is in-memory for tests/offline operation; durable distributed enforcement storage remains a production-hardening requirement.
Repository CI validation is expected to run from the PR head and must be checked before merge.
